meta.title: Batatis cost model parameters
meta.currency: CAD unless the unit says USD
meta.columns: low/base/high. For case-type parameters, low = repeat Part 9 house, base = bespoke Part 9 or small building, high = complex Part 3.
meta.kinds: published = a primary or official page states it; measured = a repo run produced it; assumed = our choice, basis in source_note

parameters.description: Building-code variance applications in Alberta per year
parameters.source_note: Low: 2023 registered building variances (837, Council says incomplete). Base: 2021-2022 average (1,698 and 1,713). High: Data Hub H1 2026 building article entries 3,088 x 2 = 6,176, a ceiling because one variance can cite several articles (https://www.safetycodes.ab.ca/data-hub/variance-data/, counts read 2026-10-20 by docs/research/2026-10-20-vision/C-market-provinces-business.md section 2.0).

parameters.description: Share of applications that are repeat Part 9 house variances
parameters.source_note: Top article 9.10.15.5.(8) is 49% of H1 2026 entries and the top five are 81%, all Part 9 section 9.10. The split is our assumption; the Council does not record variance type. Low column = most repeats.

parameters.description: Share that are bespoke Part 9 or small-building cases
parameters.source_note: Repo research assumes 5% to 15% bespoke (C-market-provinces-business.md section 2.5).

parameters.description: Share that are complex Part 3 cases needing a fire engineer
parameters.source_note: No public split exists.

parameters.description: Safety Codes Officer II hourly wage, City of Edmonton
parameters.source_note: City of Edmonton posting Apr 14, 2026, 40 h/week range C$43.923 to C$56.527; base is the midpoint. Cross-check: ALIS NOC 22233 construction inspectors average C$46.50/h, 2023 survey (https://alis.alberta.ca/occinfo/wages-and-salaries-in-alberta/construction-inspectors/22233/).

parameters.description: Benefits and overhead on top of wage
parameters.source_note: Common public-sector range; not published for Edmonton. Upper check: the Council lets the Alberta Safety Codes Authority charge C$125/h for an alternative solution or variance (https://ebs.safetycodes.ab.ca/documents/webdocs/sr/council%20fee%20schedule%20asca%20v2.pdf, effective 2022).
ACEC Saskatchewan 2026 recommended minimum rates: E1 C$160, E3 project engineer C$225, E4 specialist C$265. Saskatchewan, not Alberta; no Alberta schedule found.

parameters.description: Builder or designer staff time for repeat filings
parameters.source_note: Repo assumption C$75 to C$120 (C-market-provinces-business.md section 2.5).

parameters.description: Annual interest on money tied up in the project
parameters.source_note: Bank of Canada raised its policy rate to 2.5% on Oct 28, 2026 (published). Prime is usually policy plus 2.2 points (about 4.7%); construction loans usually price at prime plus 1 to 4 points. The spread is our assumption.

parameters.description: Money tied up while the decision waits
parameters.source_note: Low: one production house. Base: the repo business plan figure for one house. High: a small multi-unit project. Cross-check: BILD/Altus 2022 put each month of approval delay at C$2,600 per GTA apartment (Ontario, development approvals, not variances).

parameters.description: Applicant cost to prepare the first submission
parameters.source_note: No Alberta consultant fee is published. Low: 4 h of builder time at C$100. Base: inside the repo range C$3,000 to C$15,000, about 35 h at C$225. High: 150 h at C$265 for a fire-engineering case; an Australian 2026 memo puts performance-based fire engineering at 15,000 to 40,000+ (AUD, https://ccc-engineering-website.pages.dev/design-memos/fire-protection-design-cost/).

parameters.description: Officer hours on the first review
parameters.source_note: Not published in Alberta. Base anchor: Kingston, Ontario charges C$318.25/h with a C$2,000 minimum for an alternative solution, about 6.3 h of recovered review time. Toronto charges C$2,368.32 and Ottawa C$430 to C$1,080 (2026 schedules).

parameters.description: Extra "more information" rounds per application today
parameters.source_note: No Alberta figure exists. Base: Surrey, BC averaged 1.6 resubmissions on residential permits (vendor blog quoting the city); Denver accepts about 37% on first submittal (https://www.coloradopolitics.com/2026/03/09/denver-approves-4-6m-ai-powered-permit-review-contract/), which implies 1.7. High: Honolulu averaged 3.4 review cycles, 2.4 extra (Stateline, https://www.newstribune.com/news/2026/aug/21/cities-turn-to-ai-to-speed-up-housing-permitting/). These are ordinary permits, not variances. Low is our assumption for repeat filings.
Reading the resubmission and writing the request.
Priced at builder_rate (low) or engineer_rate (base, high).

CWC and WoodWorks BC Alternative Solutions Guide pp.4-6: allow one to two months for correspondence and two to four months for comments (BC guidance, not a measurement). Organizers: each round adds weeks (Challenge Scope p.2). Low is our assumption for repeat filings.

parameters.description: Share of extra rounds Batatis removes
parameters.source_note: Not measured for Batatis. Comparable AI pre-checks on ordinary permits: Seattle 35% fewer correction cycles; Honolulu 3.4 to 1.4 review cycles (city-reported via Stateline, Aug 2026).
